Jonah ran away from the presence of the Lord. Where might you be running from God?
The sailors prayed while Jonah slept. How can God's people be asleep to others' need?
The sailors feared the Lord and offered sacrifices. How did God use Jonah's failure to reach them?
God appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah. How does God rescue us even when we run?
"I called out to the Lord, out of my distress, and he answered me." When has God answered you from a low place?
"When my life was fainting away, I remembered the Lord." What brings you back to God?
"Salvation belongs to the Lord!" What does this mean to you?
The word of the Lord came to Jonah a second time. What does this show about second chances?
The whole city repented, from the greatest to the least. What does true repentance look like?
God saw their turning and relented. What does this show about God's mercy?
Jonah was angry that God was merciful. When have you struggled with God's mercy to others?
Jonah knew God was "gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love." How is this good news?
God asked, "Should not I pity Nineveh?" Who might God be asking you to care about?
